content: The Master doesn't display himself, therefore people can see his light. He doesn't assert himself, therefore he is recognized.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

In Lao Tzu's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
